turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (DOCTOR): Morning. Have a seat. What's the problem?

[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): It's a few things, and I want to explain them properly so you don't think I'm just being dramatic. I've been exhausted for months, the sort of tired where I sit in the car outside the flat and can't get myself inside, and I've been blaming the audit at work and the fact that I'm fifty-two.
[SEG0003] person_1 (DOCTOR): How many months?

[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): Six months, I nearly said, but no, it was already there before the June long weekend, so eight months. Weekends too, not only after a long day, so I can't only pin it on the office, even though the office is hectic.
[SEG0005] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Ja, about eight months. I thought it was the job as well, shame.
[SEG0006] person_1 (DOCTOR): Cold?

[SEG0007] person_2 (PATIENT): Very cold. I sleep under an extra blanket when everyone else has the fan on, and my hands are ice on the keyboard. I even bought a small heater for under the desk, and my boss thinks I've lost the plot.
[SEG0008] person_1 (DOCTOR): Weight?

[SEG0009] person_2 (PATIENT): Up, which annoys me because I'm eating less, smaller plate, no second chop at the braai. The bathroom scale said five kilos and I was ready to tell you five, but the chemist scale last Tuesday said eight, so it's eight kilos, and the work trousers don't close.
[SEG0010] person_1 (DOCTOR): Bowels?

[SEG0011] person_2 (PATIENT): Constipated the whole time, pretty much. I go every three or four days, hard, and I sit there ages. Prunes, extra water, a walk round the block, none of that has fixed it, and I know that's a lot of detail but it's been miserable.
[SEG0012] person_1 (DOCTOR): Mood?

[SEG0013] person_2 (PATIENT): Low, flat. I'm not in tears, but I don't want the Saturday braai or people over, and I told myself that's just tiredness and age, not a real mood problem. Work has been grim, so it felt like an explanation.
[SEG0014] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): She cancels plans. She's quieter than she was, hey, and she doesn't laugh at the same things.
[SEG0015] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any fever?
[SEG0016] person_2 (PATIENT): No. No fever. I've checked with the thermometer at home a few times because I feel so off, and it's always normal.
[SEG0017] person_1 (DOCTOR): Chest pain? Short of breath?
[SEG0018] person_2 (PATIENT): No chest pain, no. And not short of breath. I get up the stairs at the office fine, I just don't want to.
[SEG0019] person_1 (DOCTOR): Hair loss? Dry skin?

[SEG0020] person_2 (PATIENT): Dry skin, ja, my shins flake even with the cream from the chemist. Hair, no, I'm not losing it. A couple of strands in the shower, same as the last ten years, nothing unusual on the pillow.
[SEG0021] person_1 (DOCTOR): Periods regular?

[SEG0022] person_2 (PATIENT): Not the last year. Some months heavy, some barely there, and I put that with being fifty-two. Not pregnant either, my husband had the snip years ago, so we can leave that.
[SEG0023] person_1 (DOCTOR): Thyroid disease in the family?

[SEG0024] person_2 (PATIENT): My mother, ja. Underactive thyroid, on tablets for years, always cold, always slow, and she died in twenty nineteen from a stroke, not the thyroid. My sister's been on at me to come because she reckons I look like Mum did.
[SEG0025] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Her mum was on Eltroxin forever. Same cold hands. That's why I pushed her to book.
[SEG0026] person_1 (DOCTOR): Had a thyroid test yourself?

[SEG0027] person_2 (PATIENT): Once, at the day clinic, and they said borderline, that's the word they used. I nearly told you the TSH was 4.2, but that's wrong, the sister said five-point-something, still borderline, and no tablets. When it was, I can't tell you, ages ago, twenty nineteen or later, I honestly don't know.
[SEG0028] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): And she never went back. The paper is in a drawer at home. She hangs onto that word borderline and that's it.
[SEG0029] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any medicines now?

[SEG0030] person_2 (PATIENT): The only one I was properly on was ferrous sulphate from my GP, for this tiredness. Two hundred milligrams, I was about to say, no, it was the three hundred and twenty-five milligram tablet, once a day, by mouth. I stopped it in March because it bunged me up even more.
[SEG0031] person_1 (DOCTOR): Thyroxine ever?

[SEG0032] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Never given it, never took a single tablet. I do take a supermarket multivitamin most mornings, one tablet, nothing fancy, and I couldn't tell you the strength. No cholesterol tablets and no blood pressure tablets.
[SEG0033] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): That vitamin, she misses it more days than she takes it. The bottle hardly moves.
[SEG0034] person_2 (PATIENT): I take it when I remember, which is not every day, I'll give you that. Some weeks it's three times and then I lose track, so don't write it down as religious.
[SEG0035] person_1 (DOCTOR): Pulse is sixty-two... no, fifty-six. Thyroid isn't enlarged. Hands are cool. Skin on the shins is dry.

[SEG0036] person_2 (PATIENT): Is fifty-six a problem? I used to run half marathons and it sat low then, but I haven't trained in ages, just a walk to the robot and back, and even that feels like a mission now.
[SEG0037] person_1 (DOCTOR): Not an emergency. This could be an underactive thyroid, or it could be the workload and getting older. I'm not deciding that today.

[SEG0038] person_2 (PATIENT): If it's thyroid like my mum I want it found, and if it's just the audit and my age I don't want tablets for nothing. I've been reading online, which is silly, and half the sites say thyroid and half say burnout, so I've been going in circles for weeks.
[SEG0039] person_1 (DOCTOR): Bloods will sort the thyroid question. TSH, free T4, and a full blood count, tomorrow morning, not fasting.

[SEG0040] person_2 (PATIENT): Does the blood count cover iron? I stopped the ferrous sulphate, and nobody actually checked a level before they handed me the script, which still irritates me. If I'm anaemic that explains some of this, though not the cold, I don't think.
[SEG0041] person_1 (DOCTOR): Yes, the full blood count covers anaemia. No thyroid tablets today, and don't restart the iron.
[SEG0042] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Not even every second day?
[SEG0043] person_1 (DOCTOR): No. Leave it off. It was making the constipation worse.

[SEG0044] person_2 (PATIENT): Good, I don't want it back. On the mood, I'm not asking for an antidepressant, my cousin had a horrible time on one and I forget the name, but if the flatness needs something separate I should say so now instead of pretending I'm fine.
[SEG0045] person_1 (DOCTOR): Nothing for mood today. If the thyroid bloods are normal and you still feel flat, we'll discuss it at the review.

[SEG0046] person_2 (PATIENT): So do I come back only if it's abnormal? I don't want to take a morning off the audit for a normal result, although the cold and the eight kilos will still be there even if the TSH is lovely.
[SEG0047] person_1 (DOCTOR): Come back next week either way. We go through the results here.

[SEG0048] person_2 (PATIENT): Next week I can do Thursday, I think, not Wednesday, the auditors are in. Should I bring that old clinic printout if I find it? I might have the number wrong, five-point-something is what stuck, and they said borderline, but I wouldn't swear to the figure.
[SEG0049] person_1 (DOCTOR): Bring it if you find it. Tomorrow's test stands either way.
[SEG0050] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I'll dig in the drawer tonight. She'll never look.
[SEG0051] person_1 (DOCTOR): Sleep all right?

[SEG0052] person_2 (PATIENT): Sleep is fine once I'm warm. I drop off and I don't lie awake. I wake a bit early some mornings from the cold, but it's not insomnia, so please don't write that down as a sleep problem.
[SEG0053] person_1 (DOCTOR): Nausea, vomiting, tummy pain?

[SEG0054] person_2 (PATIENT): No nausea, no vomiting, no tummy pain. Appetite is down, that's true, food just doesn't appeal, which is why the smaller portions. The weight still went up, which is the confusing bit, and I've turned that over in my head a hundred times.
[SEG0055] person_1 (DOCTOR): Waterworks?
[SEG0056] person_2 (PATIENT): Fine. No burning, and I'm not up all night. I drink lots of water for the bowels, and rooibos, so I go a bit more in the day, but that's the fluids, not a problem.
[SEG0057] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): The rooibos is all day at her desk. And she stays till seven when the audit is on. It's not a quiet job.

[SEG0058] person_2 (PATIENT): Ja, long hours, and I sit most of the day, which doesn't help the bowels, I know that. I used to walk at lunch and I stopped that months ago. That's the whole picture, I hope I haven't gone on too long.
[SEG0059] person_1 (DOCTOR): Enough to go on. Bloods tomorrow morning at the lab, not fasting. Back here next week for the results, whatever they show.
